newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha lower amid slow end-user demand.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha lower amid slow end-user demand.

text.p: Naphtha prices moved lower in afternoon Tokyo trade on Monday due to sluggish demand from petrochemical end-users as well as crude losses in Friday's overseas markets, traders said.
Offers for second-half March open-spec naphtha were heard at $233.50 per tonne, while bids were assessed at $232.00. It was quoted at $237.00/238.00 in late trading on Friday.
First-half April was quoted at $230.00/231.50, compared with late Friday's $235.00/236.00.
In spreads, second-half March/second-half April was talked at around plus $3.50. It was traded at $3.80 on Friday.
In physical naphtha trading, end-user activity was said to be dull, with slow demand for second-half February cargoes.

In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, Indonesia is expected to announce its initial February allocation later this week, traders said. They also said the allocation for February lifting is likely to total around 3.5 million barrels.

Traders said Kuwait Petroleum Corp would have term talks with its east Asian naphtha buyers from February 17 in Singapore for a one-year term period starting in March. About a dozen term lifters, mainly from Japan and South Korea, are expected to participate in the talks. -- Tokyo Energy Desk
